title: Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani
text: This might be the toughest fight on the card to breakdown. I like Chidi a lot. He is very long, very fast, uses all of his techniques well. But seeing him be rocked in his last fight makes me think his chin could be slipping. He is 36 years old and cuts an enormous amount of weight. i am going to slight lean Jake Matthews because he is very durable and has the wrestling upside. Jake Matthews Jake Mathews is a well rounded guy withs solid wrestling, very good grappling and a nice variety of strikes. He works angles well and has no problem mixing up body shots and head shots. He averages a little more than 1 takedown per fight. He has a solid striking differential at 3-2 and very real power in his hands. He is coming off the decision win over Francisco Prado where the size difference was very helpful. Chidi Njokuani Chidi Njokuani is a very good striker with speed, power and solid distance control. He is not a high volume guy but he sticks and moves really well. His feet are never in the same place for very long and people have a really hard time getting to him. If you are able to get inside the reach and work your way to his legs you can potentially have success with takedowns. He is coming off the KO win over Elizu Zaleski where he himself, was rocked early.

title: UFC Fight Night Nashville: Odds, Predictions, and Best Bets for Saturday, July 12
text: Coming off the amazing card at UFC 317, we have a UFC Fight Night card that should provide some action down in Nashville, TN. Headlined by legendary Heavyweight Derrick Lewis taking on undefeated rising star Tallison Teixeira, Saturday night should surely be filled with some action. Today, I will break down my 3 favorite bets for this weekend’s fight card. Let’s get into it! Matthews is a veteran of the UFC at this point, with 21 fights, this being 22, under his belt. He holds a 14-7 record across his 11-year run in the UFC and is entering this fight on a 2-fight win streak. He is taking on Chidi Njokuani, who is 5-3 in his UFC career, but has made some noise as a known KO artist. Njokuani has won 3 straight coming into this one, so both fighters should be fighting with confidence. This fight is a true clash of styles. Matthews is pretty well-rounded, but he is a much stronger grappler than Chidi. Chidi comes from a Muay Thai background, and you can see it when he fights. He has brutal elbows and clean striking, which will certainly cause problems for Matthews. The biggest advantage I see for Chidi is his height and reach. Chidi stands at 6’3 with an 80” reach compared to Matthews at 5’11 with a 73” reach. I think Chidi is going to be able to keep Matthews at a distance and avoid the takedowns, all while inflicting some damage from striking range. MY PICK: Chidi Njokuani -155 It has been a brutal stretch fro Calvin Kattar. He has lost 4 straight fights and is 1-5 over his last 6. Still, Calvin is as tough as they come, and I feel as though he is going to come out firing in this one. However, he is going to have to stop the insane run of Steve Garcia. Garcia is on a 5-fight win streak with all 5 being finishes. His quality of opponents hasn’t been nearly what Calvin has faced, but 5 straight finishes in the UFC is insane. Kattar since he stepped in the octagon back in 2017, but I feel as though his career is slipping away. Losing 4 straight and now being 37, it is tough to turn things around when the UFC is handing you guys like Garcia. Garcis is a problem everywhere; he can knock you out and grapple a little bit, but he is ultra-aggressive. If Calvin can’t find his rhythm early, he may be in some serious trouble. I think Garcia wins this one, but Kattar is too tough not to go the distance. MY PICK: Steve Garcia by Decision +400 This fight is guaranteed fireworks. Derrick Lewis is one of, if not the, most prolific KO artist in UFC history. With 15 KO/TKO wins in the UFC, he has a 79% KO/TKO rate in his wins. He will now take on a 25-year-old, undefeated prospect, Tallison Teixeira. Teixeira is 8-0 and has never had an opponent make it out of the first round against him. He has had only 1 UFC fight so far, and he impressed with a TKO win over Justin Tafa at the end of Round 1. This fight is almost guaranteed to see someone go to sleep. Lewis has been around the block, which gives me some confidence, but now at 40 years old, you have to wonder if he still has his chin. For Teixeira, this is a huge jump in competition. Justin Tafa is a mid to low-tier UFC Heavyweight, and to jump from him to Lewis, who has fought some of the greatest HWs of all time, is wild. This may be a classic fast Heavyweight fight, and while it is scheduled for 5 rounds, there is almost no shot we see that. I do think both guys will be a bit cautious out of the gate, and we may see this fight slide to rounds 3-4. So, I am rolling with Teixeira to win with rounds 3-4, mainly for the value here. MY PICK: Tallison Teixeira to win in Rounds 3-4 +1200

title: UFC Nashville odds: Best betting props, parlays and picks | Lewis vs. Teixeira
text: UFC Nashville goes down this weekend (Sat., July 12, 2025) inside Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. The main event features Heavyweights with Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira. Lewis, a divisional stalwart, is hoping to get past the UFC neophyte and secure a fight with new UFC champion, Tom Aspinall. When it comes to the rest of the UFC Nashville card, there’s not too much to write home about. The co-main is Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim. Rounding out the main card is Calvin Kattar vs. Steve Garcia, Nate Landwehr vs. Morgan Charriere, Vitor Petrino vs. Austin Lane and Junior Tafa vs Tuco Tokkos. UFC Nashville’s “Prelims” are headlined by Max Griffin vs. Chris Curtis. The “Prelims” also have Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani and Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura. As always, there’s lots to bet on this card and we’ve got odds for all the fights below: UFC Nashville Main Card Money Line Odds Derrick Lewis (+220) vs. Tallison Teixeira (-270) The towering Teixeira is just 8-0 and two fights into his UFC career. He debuted in the Octagon with a Contender Series first round knockout over Arthur Lopes. In his proper debut, he put away Justin Tafa in 35 seconds (see it here). Lewis — who turned 40 this year — is coming off a third round technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento. Before that, he lost a five-round decision to Jailton Almeida. And before that, he scored a 33-second win over Marcos Rogerio Lima (see it here). That win snapped a three fight losing skid (all finishes) where he lost to Serghei Spivac, Sergei Pavlovich and Tai Tuivasa. There’s not much to scout when it comes to Teixeira. He’s very tall and very long and he’s coming into UFC in his athletic prime at only 25 years-old. Lewis is giving up four inches of height and four inches of reach to the young Brazilian. The last time Lewis fought someone with that kind of reach it was Pavlovich and he lasted just 55 seconds. Lewis is capable of the spectacular and shocking in an Octagon. But, it really feels like the odds are stacked against him here, with a fighter so long, so powerful and with so much youth on his side. Lewis’ defense against significant strikes is just 40 percent. That spells a lot of trouble for “The Black Beast” against a man who, so far, has landed 14.61 significant strikes per-minute across his three Octagon appearances. In Heavyweight, it only takes one punch to win, a lot of the times, but I have to favor the man who is going to be landing dozens of them in a round (if it makes it that far). The round total for this fight is set at 1.5. I think the under is most likely, as do many others. The odds are just -210 for that prop. Teixeira by KO/TKO/DQ is a laughable -185. And Teixeira to win by strikes in round one is just -125. Clearly, there’s not much value if you believe Teixeira is going to quickly separate Lewis from his consciousness (as I do). For my best bet, I’m going to go for a winning round and method of victory parlay. I’m taking round one and TKO/KO/DQ. This covers me just in case Lewis does something silly/outstanding in the first round in Nashville. Best bet: Fight to end in Round 1 by KO/TKO/DQ (-150) Stephen Thompson (+320) vs. Gabriel Bonfim (-410) Thompson is coming off a third round knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley (see it here). Before that, he was submitted by Shavkat Rakhmonov (see it here). His last win was over Kevin Holland, when Holland retired at the end of round four. Bonfim, on the other hand, choked out Khaos Williams in his last fight (see it here). Before that, he took a decision over Ange Loosa. Before those fights he lost, as a big favorite, to Nicolas Dalby via technical knockout (see it here). I don’t think Thompson is long for this sport. He turned 42 this year and his fighting style isn’t great for masking your age. He can’t hide behind takedowns and take dangerous finishers out of their comfort zones. He has to stand in front of them and hope he can slip strikes and land enough from range to earn a decision. Bonfim is not a dangerous striker, so I’m not worried about Thompson getting KO’d for the second time in two fights. Bonfim’s submission threat is what I’m worried about, though. Bonfim’s submissions come from all angles and at a scary pace. I don’t think Thompson will be able to fight those off for long enough to stay in the fight and will probably end up tapping from a choke. Thompson has never had elite takedown defense. With age, his 63 percent takedown defense will feel closer to 50 percent. Bonfim lands almost four takedowns per 15 minutes. He’s going to get Thompson down. Bonfim by submission is only +125. I feel strongly that this is what’s going to happen. But those odds are a little stingy. Unfortunately, the Bonfim -3.5 is even stingier at -205. For my best bet I’m going deep into DraftKings props and I’m looking at Bonfim to win in rounds one or two. I really struggle to see Thompson make it to the final bell and this at least covers me if Thompson is shot to the point that Bonfim can get him out of there with ground-and-pound. Best bet: Gabriel Bonfim to win in rounds 1-2 (+120) Calvin Kattar (+102) vs. Steve Garcia (-122) The Featherweight division have a right to be scared of Garcia. He’s one a five-fight finish streak right now, including stoppages over Melquizael Costa (see it here) and Chase Hooper (see it here). Hooper and Costa have looked pretty good since then, so that tells us what kind of level Costa has been operating at lately. Kattar, on the other hand, will lock up a rare five-fight losing streak in UFC if he gets stopped by Garcia. Last time out he was well beaten by Youssef Zalal (who won despite staying in cruise control). Before that, he was beaten by Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen (due to an injury) and Josh Emmett (split decision). Kattar’s toughness is the stuff of legend, thanks to the unholy beating he once took from Max Holloway. Kattar has never been stopped in his career (other than that knee injury). At 37, though, with all these wars in his past, is this the time we see that chin fade? I think so. Garcia’s punches land like a sock full of pennies. And I fear he’s going to land something really hard on Kattar. I think we’re going to see a technical knockout from Garcia, probably from ground-and-pound. I’ll take the point spread here on Garcia, believing that if Kattar doesn’t go down, Garcia will still take a dominant decision (also because Garcia by KO was only +165). Best bet: Steve Garcia -3.5 (+110) Nate Landwehr (+220) vs. Morgan Charriere (-270) Landwehr got styled on in his last fight. Doo Ho Choi looked incredible as he out-struck and out-wrestled and eventually finished “The Train” (see it here). Before that, Landwehr scored a comeback technical knockout on Jamall Emmers (see it here). In his early UFC career, Landwehr managed to get wins over Darren Elkins, L’udovit Klein and David Onama. Charriere, meanwhile, is coming off a unanimous decision loss to Nathaniel Wood where he looked good, not great. Before that, he blew away Gabriel Miranda with a left hook (see it here). Landwehr is a hard-nosed brawler who is willing to eat two shot to land one. He’s a bit like Elkins without the grappling (as exposed by how often Choi took and held him down). I think this is a very tough match-up for him, against Charriere who has looked good against opponents who charge at him. Both these guys absorb more significant strikes than they land (which is a big red flag for me), but Charriere’s negative differential is higher. Charriere is also giving up three inches in the reach department. Even so, I think Charriere’s counter punching will be the story of this fight. Landwehr doesn’t exactly fight behind his jab and pick his shots. He’ll be crashing forward trying to overwhelm Charriere. In this situation, I like Charriere to respond with something hard that puts Landwehr down. Charriere reminds me of a striker in football/soccer who misses the goal when he’s given too much time to think about his shot, but who can score on instinct when the ball comes to him and he has to react without thinking. That’s how I see Charriere getting his finish here. Best bet: Morgan Charriere moneyline (-220) Vitor Petrino (-700) vs. Austen Lane (+500) Petrino’s shiny 11-0 record was dulled by Anthony Smith and Dustin Jacoby last year. Smith scored a quick guillotine on the Brazilian (see it here) in Brazil. Then Jacoby scored a late knockout in a very boring fight (see it here). Lane, meanwhile, was KO’d by Mario Pinto last time out (see it here). Before that, he successfully fraud checked Robelis Despaigne. Prior to that fight, he was starched by Jhonata Diniz (see it here). If it wasn’t for Tuco Tokkos, Lane might be the worst fighter on a UFC main card this year. Lane has a terrible 40 percent defense on significant strikes. That’s a death sentence at Heavyweight. For the most part in his career, big shots have been able to find Lane and he’s been stopped more than your average bear (all six of his defeats are by knockout). He’s been stopped so much, that you wonder whether the 37 year old should still get a license. But, this is MMA, right? We’ll let anyone fight. Petrino came to UFC with a reputation for vicious striking, but we’ve not seen much of that in the Octagon. What we have seen has been pretty slow and telegraphed. Is that still too fast and unpredictable for Lane, though? Lane has a decent-size advantage against Petrino and I can actually see him taking Petrino down and laying on him for a round or two. However, whenever they are standing I’m worried that Lane is one punch away from being laid out. This is what we saw in the Diniz fight. Since they start rounds standing, I have to give this to Petrino. I’m not very enthusiastic about the pick, though. The round total is 1.5. I’ll go with the over, thinking Lane will get his early takedown and Petrino will continue to underwhelm, even in a winning effort. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+135) Junior Tafa (-166) vs. Tuco Tokkos (+140) Tafa put away super short notice opponent Sean Sharaf back in Oct. 2024. That was his first fight since being heel hooked by Valter Walker (who fights further down the card). Before that, Tafa was TKO’d by Marcos Rogerio de Lima (see it here). Tokkos, meanwhile, stifled Navajo Stirling last time out, losing just by decision to the super hyped prospect. Before that he was submitted by Oumar Sy, with Sy locking up the rear-naked choke when Tokkos was mugging for the commentary booth. Tokkos, as referenced earlier, is probably the worst main card fighter of the year. He’s not shown us much of anything thus far in his UFC career. He did well to hang in there against Stirling, but he offered very little offensive threat. Stirling’s passivity was mostly to blame for that awful fight going the distance. Tafa isn’t much better. He’s 2-3 in UFC and the two guys he beat are well below UFC quality. I think Tafa wins this, thanks to how hittable Tokkos is (4.99 significant strikes absorbed per minute and just 33 percent significant strike defense). I wouldn’t be surprised if we get another stinker, though, that goes the distance with a decision that could go to either guy. Because I’m not sold on Tafa, over 1.5 rounds looks quite appealing. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+105) UFC Nashville ‘Prelims’ Under Card Odds Max Griffin (+250) vs. Chris Curtis (-310) This is our featured “Prelim”? I guess this slot really is just, “the fight before the main card” now. The 39-year-old Griffin was tapped by Michael Chiesa in Dec. 2024. He’s been win-loss-win-loss for the past few years, with the wins being split decisions over Jeremiah Wells and Tim Means. The 37-year-old Curtis is coming off trying to separate Sean Strickland from some dude in a regional MMA cage. In his last UFC fight, Curtis lost a controversial fight with Roman Kopylov (see it here). That fight was officially ruled a head kick knockout loss at 4:59 of round three. Many felt the fight could have been left for the remaining second and then have the judges decide (I scored it for Kopylov anyways). Griffin is an okay striker and wrestler, but at 39, his potency in either area needs to be questioned. Curtis, who isn’t much younger, seems to still be a reliable and creative volume striker. His very good takedown defense probably holds up to the level needed to stay up against Griffin, too. I think there’s a chance Curtis gets a stoppage in this fight, but it might come late. I’m not going to mess around with any round betting here and instead just go with Curtis on the moneyline. Best bet: Chris Curtis moneyline (-310) Jake Matthews (+124) vs. Chidi Njokuani (-148) Both these guys are on good runs and coming off decisive wins. It’s a little surprising to see them matched up here on the “Prelims.” Matthews beat Francisco Prado by unanimous decision in February. Last year, he defeated Phil Rowe. Prior to that, he managed to make it to a losing decision against the undefeated Michael Morales. Njokuani, meanwhile, lit up Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos on the co-main of an APEX card in March (see it here). He did miss weight for that one, though. Prior to that TKO he beat Jared Gooden and Rhys McKee. Njokuani is very big for the weight class. He’s four inches taller than Matthews and will have a long seven-inch reach advantage. That reach could be significant, as it was in Njokuani’s destruction of Dos Santos. Njokuani’s reach gets even more deadlier when you consider he has the best accuracy rate for sig. strikes in the division at 62 percent. The only reason he isn’t the official leader in that stat at Welterweight is because his last two fights have technically been Catchweights (due to his weigh-in misses). The 62 percent is better than Gunnar Nelson’s official best mark of 60.6 percent and all the other killers in this rejuvenated weight class. Matthews is no slouch, though. He’s an intelligent and well rounded fighter. He probably knows he can’t win a kickboxing match and I think he’s going to try and make this an ugly brawl against the fence. He’ll look to grind on Njokuani and land a few takedowns. That might be tough, though, given Njokuani’s 75 percent takedown defense. Ultimately, I think Njokuani is going to prevent himself getting taken down in this fight. And, if Matthews, won’t let him strike from range, I still think Njokuani has a good shot at landing heavy strikes right inside Matthews’ kitchen. Njokuani’s Muay Thai style is perfect for clinch fighting, so he might find a home for some good elbows and knees. The round total for this one is set at 1.5 for some reason. The over on that is -298, so no value there. And I don’t think there’s a finish in this fight. I’ll just go with the Njokuani moneyline. Best bet: Chidi Njokuani moneyline (-148) Lauren Murphy (+440) vs. Eduarda Moura (-600) Murphy has been out of action since her bruising loss to Jessica Andrade in Jan. 2023. Before that, she dominated the un-retired Miesha Tate. Before those fights, she was TKO’d while trying to get the belt off Valentina Shevchenko. Moura, meanwhile, took a decision over Veronica Hardy in her Flyweight debut last year. That fight came after she misses weight in back-to-back Strawweight bouts. I get that Murphy has been out awhile, and that she’s 42, but Vegas is showing a lot of faith in Moura with these lines. Despite her age and inactivity as of late, I bet Murphy still “has that dog in her” and I think she will bring a lot of pressure to Moura. Moura has managed to package together wins thanks to her takedowns. Murphy’s takedown defense has been solid over her career (69 percent). The big question is whether Murphy still has good takedown defense or not. If she keeps this fight standing I think she has a good chance to take a close decision. If she is taken down, I think Moura should be able to keep her down and get a pretty comfortable decision. Either way, I think we’re going to decision. Best bet: Over 2.5 rounds (-330) Kennedy Nzechukwu (-205) vs. Valter Walker (+170) Nzechukwu is undefeated (2-0) in UFC’s Heavyweight division. In Dec. 2024, he scored a first round technical knockout over Lukasz Brzeski (see it here). Walker, on the other hand, lost to Brzeski, by decision, in his UFC debut. Since then he’s heel hooked both Junior Tafa (who didn’t like it one bit) and Don’Tale Mayes. Nzechukwu’s striking should be too much for Walker to handle. However, Nzechukwu is a little ungainly and I can totally see him getting caught by Walker’s leg locks, perhaps even after scoring a knockdown. This match-up really seems ripe for some Heavyweight nuttiness. I think it’s best to play the under in this situation, especially with the round total set at 2.5 (I was sure it would be 1.5). Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-105) Mitch Ramirez (+700) vs. Mike Davis (-1000) Ramirez was stopped by Thiago Moises leg kicks in his last fight (see those here). His only other Octagon appearance was a walloping from Carlos Prates on Contender Series. In the opposite corner, Davis returned from a year long lay-off to fight Fares Ziam in February. He looked out of sorts and was possibly carrying an injury in that fight. He seemed to be trying to minimize damage more so than win a fight. That unanimous decision was his first UFC loss since being submitted by Gilbert Burns in 2019. He’s won four UFC fights between those losses. If the Davis we’re used to seeing shows up, then he should win this without too much trouble (as reflected in those betting lines). I think we’ll see the good version of Davis in this fight and if that happens, then his funky grappling should lead to a convincing win, probably by stoppage. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-180) Fatima Kline (-1200) vs. Melissa Martinez (+750) Kline was fed to the wolves on her UFC debut, coming in on short notice and up a weight class to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius. She got dominated by the bigger fighter in that bout, but rebounded with a technical knockout over Victoria Dudakova (see it here). Prior to joining UFC, Kline was a champ in the CFFC organization. She also has BJJ black belt under Mike Wacker. Martinez, meanwhile, is 1-1 in UFC with a decision win over Alice Ardelean and a decision loss to Elise Reed. She’s a former champ in the Combate organization. Martinez — who is just 5’2” — should be fighting at Atomweight (and UFC should have an Atomweight division). Kline is going to have a lot of size and strength over her (not much reach, though). I think that size difference will be most notable on the ground and I think Kline is going to use that to get a submission. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (+114) UFC Nashville Long Shots! Here’s a couple of long shots for Saturday night’s action. Derrick Lewis to Win and Over 3.5 (+1000) Let’s just imagine that Teixeira is being over-hyped and that his best work has all come against tomato cans. And let’s imagine that Lewis is going to rewind the clock and survive a lot of early punishment. Maybe Teixeira punches himself out? And then, maybe Lewis uncorks one of his classic right hooks that knocks him out cold? It’s not impossible, right? It’s Heavyweight after all. Three-fight parlay: Tallison Teixeira, Steve Garcia, Valter Walker (+568) Despite that first long shot bet, I’m reasonably confident that Teixeira is legit enough to be better than a 40-year-old Lewis. I’m also pretty confident that Steve Garcia will add to his impressive winning streak when he meets Kattar. Walker is my wild card in this parlay and he’s here to add some value. Nzechukwu has looked good at Heavyweight so far, but he’s not faced anyone like Walker. Morgan Charriere to win by KO/TKO/DQ and over 1.5 rounds (+550) I used DraftKings to make my own same game parlay here. It kind of kills me to do it, since I really like Landwehr. Unfortunately, I just think he will fight right into Charriere’s strengths and walk into something nasty. title: Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani
text: This might be the toughest fight on the card to breakdown. I like Chidi a lot. He is very long, very fast, uses all of his techniques well. But seeing him be rocked in his last fight makes me think his chin could be slipping. He is 36 years old and cuts an enormous amount of weight. i am going to slight lean Jake Matthews because he is very durable and has the wrestling upside. Jake Matthews Jake Mathews is a well rounded guy withs solid wrestling, very good grappling and a nice variety of strikes. He works angles well and has no problem mixing up body shots and head shots. He averages a little more than 1 takedown per fight. He has a solid striking differential at 3-2 and very real power in his hands. He is coming off the decision win over Francisco Prado where the size difference was very helpful. Chidi Njokuani Chidi Njokuani is a very good striker with speed, power and solid distance control. He is not a high volume guy but he sticks and moves really well. His feet are never in the same place for very long and people have a really hard time getting to him. If you are able to get inside the reach and work your way to his legs you can potentially have success with takedowns. He is coming off the KO win over Elizu Zaleski where he himself, was rocked early.

title: Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani Among UFC Nashville Additions
text: July’s UFC Nashville card continues to grow, and with the card’s heavyweight main event recently announced, promotion officials have confirmed more bouts – including Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani at welterweight. News of the bout, and several others, was revealed in a press release issued on Tuesday. The event takes place on July 12, 2025 at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, TN with Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira headlining. Once the youngest fighter on the UFC roster, Australia’s Matthews (21-7) is now thirty, and riding high on a two-fight win streak. title: UFC Fight Night Nashville: Odds, Predictions, and Best Bets for Saturday, July 12
text: Coming off the amazing card at UFC 317, we have a UFC Fight Night card that should provide some action down in Nashville, TN. Headlined by legendary Heavyweight Derrick Lewis taking on undefeated rising star Tallison Teixeira, Saturday night should surely be filled with some action. Today, I will break down my 3 favorite bets for this weekend’s fight card. Let’s get into it! Matthews is a veteran of the UFC at this point, with 21 fights, this being 22, under his belt. He holds a 14-7 record across his 11-year run in the UFC and is entering this fight on a 2-fight win streak. He is taking on Chidi Njokuani, who is 5-3 in his UFC career, but has made some noise as a known KO artist. Njokuani has won 3 straight coming into this one, so both fighters should be fighting with confidence. This fight is a true clash of styles. Matthews is pretty well-rounded, but he is a much stronger grappler than Chidi. Chidi comes from a Muay Thai background, and you can see it when he fights. He has brutal elbows and clean striking, which will certainly cause problems for Matthews. The biggest advantage I see for Chidi is his height and reach. Chidi stands at 6’3 with an 80” reach compared to Matthews at 5’11 with a 73” reach. I think Chidi is going to be able to keep Matthews at a distance and avoid the takedowns, all while inflicting some damage from striking range. MY PICK: Chidi Njokuani -155 It has been a brutal stretch fro Calvin Kattar. He has lost 4 straight fights and is 1-5 over his last 6. Still, Calvin is as tough as they come, and I feel as though he is going to come out firing in this one. However, he is going to have to stop the insane run of Steve Garcia. Garcia is on a 5-fight win streak with all 5 being finishes. His quality of opponents hasn’t been nearly what Calvin has faced, but 5 straight finishes in the UFC is insane. Kattar since he stepped in the octagon back in 2017, but I feel as though his career is slipping away. Losing 4 straight and now being 37, it is tough to turn things around when the UFC is handing you guys like Garcia. Garcis is a problem everywhere; he can knock you out and grapple a little bit, but he is ultra-aggressive. If Calvin can’t find his rhythm early, he may be in some serious trouble. I think Garcia wins this one, but Kattar is too tough not to go the distance. MY PICK: Steve Garcia by Decision +400 This fight is guaranteed fireworks. Derrick Lewis is one of, if not the, most prolific KO artist in UFC history. With 15 KO/TKO wins in the UFC, he has a 79% KO/TKO rate in his wins. He will now take on a 25-year-old, undefeated prospect, Tallison Teixeira. Teixeira is 8-0 and has never had an opponent make it out of the first round against him. He has had only 1 UFC fight so far, and he impressed with a TKO win over Justin Tafa at the end of Round 1. This fight is almost guaranteed to see someone go to sleep. Lewis has been around the block, which gives me some confidence, but now at 40 years old, you have to wonder if he still has his chin. For Teixeira, this is a huge jump in competition. Justin Tafa is a mid to low-tier UFC Heavyweight, and to jump from him to Lewis, who has fought some of the greatest HWs of all time, is wild. This may be a classic fast Heavyweight fight, and while it is scheduled for 5 rounds, there is almost no shot we see that. I do think both guys will be a bit cautious out of the gate, and we may see this fight slide to rounds 3-4. So, I am rolling with Teixeira to win with rounds 3-4, mainly for the value here. MY PICK: Tallison Teixeira to win in Rounds 3-4 +1200

title: UFC Nashville odds: Best betting props, parlays and picks | Lewis vs. Teixeira
text: UFC Nashville goes down this weekend (Sat., July 12, 2025) inside Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. The main event features Heavyweights with Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira. Lewis, a divisional stalwart, is hoping to get past the UFC neophyte and secure a fight with new UFC champion, Tom Aspinall. When it comes to the rest of the UFC Nashville card, there’s not too much to write home about. The co-main is Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim. Rounding out the main card is Calvin Kattar vs. Steve Garcia, Nate Landwehr vs. Morgan Charriere, Vitor Petrino vs. Austin Lane and Junior Tafa vs Tuco Tokkos. UFC Nashville’s “Prelims” are headlined by Max Griffin vs. Chris Curtis. The “Prelims” also have Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani and Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura. As always, there’s lots to bet on this card and we’ve got odds for all the fights below: UFC Nashville Main Card Money Line Odds Derrick Lewis (+220) vs. Tallison Teixeira (-270) The towering Teixeira is just 8-0 and two fights into his UFC career. He debuted in the Octagon with a Contender Series first round knockout over Arthur Lopes. In his proper debut, he put away Justin Tafa in 35 seconds (see it here). Lewis — who turned 40 this year — is coming off a third round technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento. Before that, he lost a five-round decision to Jailton Almeida. And before that, he scored a 33-second win over Marcos Rogerio Lima (see it here). That win snapped a three fight losing skid (all finishes) where he lost to Serghei Spivac, Sergei Pavlovich and Tai Tuivasa. There’s not much to scout when it comes to Teixeira. He’s very tall and very long and he’s coming into UFC in his athletic prime at only 25 years-old. Lewis is giving up four inches of height and four inches of reach to the young Brazilian. The last time Lewis fought someone with that kind of reach it was Pavlovich and he lasted just 55 seconds. Lewis is capable of the spectacular and shocking in an Octagon. But, it really feels like the odds are stacked against him here, with a fighter so long, so powerful and with so much youth on his side. Lewis’ defense against significant strikes is just 40 percent. That spells a lot of trouble for “The Black Beast” against a man who, so far, has landed 14.61 significant strikes per-minute across his three Octagon appearances. In Heavyweight, it only takes one punch to win, a lot of the times, but I have to favor the man who is going to be landing dozens of them in a round (if it makes it that far). The round total for this fight is set at 1.5. I think the under is most likely, as do many others. The odds are just -210 for that prop. Teixeira by KO/TKO/DQ is a laughable -185. And Teixeira to win by strikes in round one is just -125. Clearly, there’s not much value if you believe Teixeira is going to quickly separate Lewis from his consciousness (as I do). For my best bet, I’m going to go for a winning round and method of victory parlay. I’m taking round one and TKO/KO/DQ. This covers me just in case Lewis does something silly/outstanding in the first round in Nashville. Best bet: Fight to end in Round 1 by KO/TKO/DQ (-150) Stephen Thompson (+320) vs. Gabriel Bonfim (-410) Thompson is coming off a third round knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley (see it here). Before that, he was submitted by Shavkat Rakhmonov (see it here). His last win was over Kevin Holland, when Holland retired at the end of round four. Bonfim, on the other hand, choked out Khaos Williams in his last fight (see it here). Before that, he took a decision over Ange Loosa. Before those fights he lost, as a big favorite, to Nicolas Dalby via technical knockout (see it here). I don’t think Thompson is long for this sport. He turned 42 this year and his fighting style isn’t great for masking your age. He can’t hide behind takedowns and take dangerous finishers out of their comfort zones. He has to stand in front of them and hope he can slip strikes and land enough from range to earn a decision. Bonfim is not a dangerous striker, so I’m not worried about Thompson getting KO’d for the second time in two fights. Bonfim’s submission threat is what I’m worried about, though. Bonfim’s submissions come from all angles and at a scary pace. I don’t think Thompson will be able to fight those off for long enough to stay in the fight and will probably end up tapping from a choke. Thompson has never had elite takedown defense. With age, his 63 percent takedown defense will feel closer to 50 percent. Bonfim lands almost four takedowns per 15 minutes. He’s going to get Thompson down. Bonfim by submission is only +125. I feel strongly that this is what’s going to happen. But those odds are a little stingy. Unfortunately, the Bonfim -3.5 is even stingier at -205. For my best bet I’m going deep into DraftKings props and I’m looking at Bonfim to win in rounds one or two. I really struggle to see Thompson make it to the final bell and this at least covers me if Thompson is shot to the point that Bonfim can get him out of there with ground-and-pound. Best bet: Gabriel Bonfim to win in rounds 1-2 (+120) Calvin Kattar (+102) vs. Steve Garcia (-122) The Featherweight division have a right to be scared of Garcia. He’s one a five-fight finish streak right now, including stoppages over Melquizael Costa (see it here) and Chase Hooper (see it here). Hooper and Costa have looked pretty good since then, so that tells us what kind of level Costa has been operating at lately. Kattar, on the other hand, will lock up a rare five-fight losing streak in UFC if he gets stopped by Garcia. Last time out he was well beaten by Youssef Zalal (who won despite staying in cruise control). Before that, he was beaten by Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen (due to an injury) and Josh Emmett (split decision). Kattar’s toughness is the stuff of legend, thanks to the unholy beating he once took from Max Holloway. Kattar has never been stopped in his career (other than that knee injury). At 37, though, with all these wars in his past, is this the time we see that chin fade? I think so. Garcia’s punches land like a sock full of pennies. And I fear he’s going to land something really hard on Kattar. I think we’re going to see a technical knockout from Garcia, probably from ground-and-pound. I’ll take the point spread here on Garcia, believing that if Kattar doesn’t go down, Garcia will still take a dominant decision (also because Garcia by KO was only +165). Best bet: Steve Garcia -3.5 (+110) Nate Landwehr (+220) vs. Morgan Charriere (-270) Landwehr got styled on in his last fight. Doo Ho Choi looked incredible as he out-struck and out-wrestled and eventually finished “The Train” (see it here). Before that, Landwehr scored a comeback technical knockout on Jamall Emmers (see it here). In his early UFC career, Landwehr managed to get wins over Darren Elkins, L’udovit Klein and David Onama. Charriere, meanwhile, is coming off a unanimous decision loss to Nathaniel Wood where he looked good, not great. Before that, he blew away Gabriel Miranda with a left hook (see it here). Landwehr is a hard-nosed brawler who is willing to eat two shot to land one. He’s a bit like Elkins without the grappling (as exposed by how often Choi took and held him down). I think this is a very tough match-up for him, against Charriere who has looked good against opponents who charge at him. Both these guys absorb more significant strikes than they land (which is a big red flag for me), but Charriere’s negative differential is higher. Charriere is also giving up three inches in the reach department. Even so, I think Charriere’s counter punching will be the story of this fight. Landwehr doesn’t exactly fight behind his jab and pick his shots. He’ll be crashing forward trying to overwhelm Charriere. In this situation, I like Charriere to respond with something hard that puts Landwehr down. Charriere reminds me of a striker in football/soccer who misses the goal when he’s given too much time to think about his shot, but who can score on instinct when the ball comes to him and he has to react without thinking. That’s how I see Charriere getting his finish here. Best bet: Morgan Charriere moneyline (-220) Vitor Petrino (-700) vs. Austen Lane (+500) Petrino’s shiny 11-0 record was dulled by Anthony Smith and Dustin Jacoby last year. Smith scored a quick guillotine on the Brazilian (see it here) in Brazil. Then Jacoby scored a late knockout in a very boring fight (see it here). Lane, meanwhile, was KO’d by Mario Pinto last time out (see it here). Before that, he successfully fraud checked Robelis Despaigne. Prior to that fight, he was starched by Jhonata Diniz (see it here). If it wasn’t for Tuco Tokkos, Lane might be the worst fighter on a UFC main card this year. Lane has a terrible 40 percent defense on significant strikes. That’s a death sentence at Heavyweight. For the most part in his career, big shots have been able to find Lane and he’s been stopped more than your average bear (all six of his defeats are by knockout). He’s been stopped so much, that you wonder whether the 37 year old should still get a license. But, this is MMA, right? We’ll let anyone fight. Petrino came to UFC with a reputation for vicious striking, but we’ve not seen much of that in the Octagon. What we have seen has been pretty slow and telegraphed. Is that still too fast and unpredictable for Lane, though? Lane has a decent-size advantage against Petrino and I can actually see him taking Petrino down and laying on him for a round or two. However, whenever they are standing I’m worried that Lane is one punch away from being laid out. This is what we saw in the Diniz fight. Since they start rounds standing, I have to give this to Petrino. I’m not very enthusiastic about the pick, though. The round total is 1.5. I’ll go with the over, thinking Lane will get his early takedown and Petrino will continue to underwhelm, even in a winning effort. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+135) Junior Tafa (-166) vs. Tuco Tokkos (+140) Tafa put away super short notice opponent Sean Sharaf back in Oct. 2024. That was his first fight since being heel hooked by Valter Walker (who fights further down the card). Before that, Tafa was TKO’d by Marcos Rogerio de Lima (see it here). Tokkos, meanwhile, stifled Navajo Stirling last time out, losing just by decision to the super hyped prospect. Before that he was submitted by Oumar Sy, with Sy locking up the rear-naked choke when Tokkos was mugging for the commentary booth. Tokkos, as referenced earlier, is probably the worst main card fighter of the year. He’s not shown us much of anything thus far in his UFC career. He did well to hang in there against Stirling, but he offered very little offensive threat. Stirling’s passivity was mostly to blame for that awful fight going the distance. Tafa isn’t much better. He’s 2-3 in UFC and the two guys he beat are well below UFC quality. I think Tafa wins this, thanks to how hittable Tokkos is (4.99 significant strikes absorbed per minute and just 33 percent significant strike defense). I wouldn’t be surprised if we get another stinker, though, that goes the distance with a decision that could go to either guy. Because I’m not sold on Tafa, over 1.5 rounds looks quite appealing. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+105) UFC Nashville ‘Prelims’ Under Card Odds Max Griffin (+250) vs. Chris Curtis (-310) This is our featured “Prelim”? I guess this slot really is just, “the fight before the main card” now. The 39-year-old Griffin was tapped by Michael Chiesa in Dec. 2024. He’s been win-loss-win-loss for the past few years, with the wins being split decisions over Jeremiah Wells and Tim Means. The 37-year-old Curtis is coming off trying to separate Sean Strickland from some dude in a regional MMA cage. In his last UFC fight, Curtis lost a controversial fight with Roman Kopylov (see it here). That fight was officially ruled a head kick knockout loss at 4:59 of round three. Many felt the fight could have been left for the remaining second and then have the judges decide (I scored it for Kopylov anyways). Griffin is an okay striker and wrestler, but at 39, his potency in either area needs to be questioned. Curtis, who isn’t much younger, seems to still be a reliable and creative volume striker. His very good takedown defense probably holds up to the level needed to stay up against Griffin, too. I think there’s a chance Curtis gets a stoppage in this fight, but it might come late. I’m not going to mess around with any round betting here and instead just go with Curtis on the moneyline. Best bet: Chris Curtis moneyline (-310) Jake Matthews (+124) vs. Chidi Njokuani (-148) Both these guys are on good runs and coming off decisive wins. It’s a little surprising to see them matched up here on the “Prelims.” Matthews beat Francisco Prado by unanimous decision in February. Last year, he defeated Phil Rowe. Prior to that, he managed to make it to a losing decision against the undefeated Michael Morales. Njokuani, meanwhile, lit up Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos on the co-main of an APEX card in March (see it here). He did miss weight for that one, though. Prior to that TKO he beat Jared Gooden and Rhys McKee. Njokuani is very big for the weight class. He’s four inches taller than Matthews and will have a long seven-inch reach advantage. That reach could be significant, as it was in Njokuani’s destruction of Dos Santos. Njokuani’s reach gets even more deadlier when you consider he has the best accuracy rate for sig. strikes in the division at 62 percent. The only reason he isn’t the official leader in that stat at Welterweight is because his last two fights have technically been Catchweights (due to his weigh-in misses). The 62 percent is better than Gunnar Nelson’s official best mark of 60.6 percent and all the other killers in this rejuvenated weight class. Matthews is no slouch, though. He’s an intelligent and well rounded fighter. He probably knows he can’t win a kickboxing match and I think he’s going to try and make this an ugly brawl against the fence. He’ll look to grind on Njokuani and land a few takedowns. That might be tough, though, given Njokuani’s 75 percent takedown defense. Ultimately, I think Njokuani is going to prevent himself getting taken down in this fight. And, if Matthews, won’t let him strike from range, I still think Njokuani has a good shot at landing heavy strikes right inside Matthews’ kitchen. Njokuani’s Muay Thai style is perfect for clinch fighting, so he might find a home for some good elbows and knees. The round total for this one is set at 1.5 for some reason. The over on that is -298, so no value there. And I don’t think there’s a finish in this fight. I’ll just go with the Njokuani moneyline. Best bet: Chidi Njokuani moneyline (-148) Lauren Murphy (+440) vs. Eduarda Moura (-600) Murphy has been out of action since her bruising loss to Jessica Andrade in Jan. 2023. Before that, she dominated the un-retired Miesha Tate. Before those fights, she was TKO’d while trying to get the belt off Valentina Shevchenko. Moura, meanwhile, took a decision over Veronica Hardy in her Flyweight debut last year. That fight came after she misses weight in back-to-back Strawweight bouts. I get that Murphy has been out awhile, and that she’s 42, but Vegas is showing a lot of faith in Moura with these lines. Despite her age and inactivity as of late, I bet Murphy still “has that dog in her” and I think she will bring a lot of pressure to Moura. Moura has managed to package together wins thanks to her takedowns. Murphy’s takedown defense has been solid over her career (69 percent). The big question is whether Murphy still has good takedown defense or not. If she keeps this fight standing I think she has a good chance to take a close decision. If she is taken down, I think Moura should be able to keep her down and get a pretty comfortable decision. Either way, I think we’re going to decision. Best bet: Over 2.5 rounds (-330) Kennedy Nzechukwu (-205) vs. Valter Walker (+170) Nzechukwu is undefeated (2-0) in UFC’s Heavyweight division. In Dec. 2024, he scored a first round technical knockout over Lukasz Brzeski (see it here). Walker, on the other hand, lost to Brzeski, by decision, in his UFC debut. Since then he’s heel hooked both Junior Tafa (who didn’t like it one bit) and Don’Tale Mayes. Nzechukwu’s striking should be too much for Walker to handle. However, Nzechukwu is a little ungainly and I can totally see him getting caught by Walker’s leg locks, perhaps even after scoring a knockdown. This match-up really seems ripe for some Heavyweight nuttiness. I think it’s best to play the under in this situation, especially with the round total set at 2.5 (I was sure it would be 1.5). Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-105) Mitch Ramirez (+700) vs. Mike Davis (-1000) Ramirez was stopped by Thiago Moises leg kicks in his last fight (see those here). His only other Octagon appearance was a walloping from Carlos Prates on Contender Series. In the opposite corner, Davis returned from a year long lay-off to fight Fares Ziam in February. He looked out of sorts and was possibly carrying an injury in that fight. He seemed to be trying to minimize damage more so than win a fight. That unanimous decision was his first UFC loss since being submitted by Gilbert Burns in 2019. He’s won four UFC fights between those losses. If the Davis we’re used to seeing shows up, then he should win this without too much trouble (as reflected in those betting lines). I think we’ll see the good version of Davis in this fight and if that happens, then his funky grappling should lead to a convincing win, probably by stoppage. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-180) Fatima Kline (-1200) vs. Melissa Martinez (+750) Kline was fed to the wolves on her UFC debut, coming in on short notice and up a weight class to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius. She got dominated by the bigger fighter in that bout, but rebounded with a technical knockout over Victoria Dudakova (see it here). Prior to joining UFC, Kline was a champ in the CFFC organization. She also has BJJ black belt under Mike Wacker. Martinez, meanwhile, is 1-1 in UFC with a decision win over Alice Ardelean and a decision loss to Elise Reed. She’s a former champ in the Combate organization. Martinez — who is just 5’2” — should be fighting at Atomweight (and UFC should have an Atomweight division). Kline is going to have a lot of size and strength over her (not much reach, though). I think that size difference will be most notable on the ground and I think Kline is going to use that to get a submission. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (+114) UFC Nashville Long Shots! Here’s a couple of long shots for Saturday night’s action. Derrick Lewis to Win and Over 3.5 (+1000) Let’s just imagine that Teixeira is being over-hyped and that his best work has all come against tomato cans. And let’s imagine that Lewis is going to rewind the clock and survive a lot of early punishment. Maybe Teixeira punches himself out? And then, maybe Lewis uncorks one of his classic right hooks that knocks him out cold? It’s not impossible, right? It’s Heavyweight after all. Three-fight parlay: Tallison Teixeira, Steve Garcia, Valter Walker (+568) Despite that first long shot bet, I’m reasonably confident that Teixeira is legit enough to be better than a 40-year-old Lewis. I’m also pretty confident that Steve Garcia will add to his impressive winning streak when he meets Kattar. Walker is my wild card in this parlay and he’s here to add some value. Nzechukwu has looked good at Heavyweight so far, but he’s not faced anyone like Walker. Morgan Charriere to win by KO/TKO/DQ and over 1.5 rounds (+550) I used DraftKings to make my own same game parlay here. It kind of kills me to do it, since I really like Landwehr. Unfortunately, I just think he will fight right into Charriere’s strengths and walk into something nasty. title: UFC on ESPN 70 gets Chris Curtis, Jake Matthews among other Nashville fight card additions
text: UFC on ESPN 70 gets Chris Curtis, Jake Matthews among other Nashville fight card additions Several bouts have been added to July's UFC on ESPN 70 in Nashville. The UFC's seventh visit to Nashville, Tenn. is taking shape. Three new bouts have been added to UFC on ESPN 70 including Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani, Max Griffin vs. Chris Curtis, and Junior Tafa vs. Ateba Gautier. The promotion announced the news Tuesday. UFC on ESPN 70 takes place July 12 at the Bridgestone Arena and is headlined by a heavyweight bout between former title challenger Derrick Lewis against undefeated prospect Tallison Teixeira. Njokuani (25-10 MMA, 5-3 UFC) looks to build on his 3-0 run since he dropped back down to welterweight. Meanwhile, Matthews (21-7 MMA, 14-7 UFC), a veteran of the weight class, looks to get his own 3-0 run, as he's coming off back-to-back decision wins over Phil Rowe and Francisco Prado. Additionally, Max Griffin welcomes Chris Curtis back to welterweight. Curtis (31-12 MMA, 5-4 UFC), who's competed all of his 10 UFC fights at 185 pounds, will be making his promotional welterweight debut. He looks to snap a two-fight losing skid now in a new division. "Pain" Griffin is 2-2 in his past four trips to the octagon, with his most recent one being a submission loss to Michael Chiesa in December at UFC 310. Lastly, Tafa (6-3 MMA, 2-3 UFC) will also be trying out a new weight class – light heavyweight. He takes on Gautier (7-1 MMA, 1-0 UFC), who's coming off a devastating KO win in his debut fight against Jose Medina in Mexico City in March.

title: Max Griffin vs Chris Curtis Pick, 07/12/2025 Predictions UFC Nashville Odds

The moneyline has Griffin priced at +250 while Curtis is at -320. Max "Pain" Griffin comes into this bout holding a record of 20-11-0. The 39-year-old will fight at 170 lbs and measures in at 5'11". The orthodox fighter stretches 76". Chris "Action-Man" Curtis stands in at 5'10" and weighs in at 170 lbs. The orthodox fighter looks to add a win to his career total of 31-12-0 (1 NC). The 37-year-old has a wingspan of 75". With respect to significant strikes, Max Griffin is connecting on 3.75 per minute and Chris Curtis connects on 6.16 significant strikes per min. Griffin is connecting on 48% of the significant strikes he throws while Curtis lands 51%. In terms of defending themselves, "Pain" absorbs 3.66 significant strikes per min and "Action-Man" allows 6.43. Chiesa ended up landing 54 of 87 total strikes that he let go in that contest. Griffin ended the night having landed 18 of 43 total strikes. In terms of significant strikes, Chiesa ended up landing 13 of 39 , which means his percentage was 33%. He finished the fight landing 11 of 33 significant strikes to the head. title: Preview: UFC Nashville Prelims - Matthews vs. Njokuani
text: Preview: UFC Nashville Prelims Matthews vs. Njokuani Welterweights Jake Matthews (21-7, 14-7 UFC) vs. Chidi Njokuani (25-10, 1 NC; 5-3 UFC)ODDS: Njokuani (-150); Matthews (+125) Advertisement In broad strokes, Matthews’ game remains the same as it ever was. He is a strong and savvy grappler who is capable everywhere but does his best work from top position, and while his striking shows decent power and has improved incrementally over the years, it remains awkward-looking and defensively porous. That being the case, Matthews’ fights tend to hinge on who is the better wrestler, as takedowns are an important safety valve for when things are not going his way on the feet, and present his best chance to get the fight to the ground in the time, place and position of his choosing. It is a fairly straightforward calculus of victory that Matthews sometimes makes more complicated by underusing his wrestling. Njokuani is, in many ways, the polar opposite of Matthews. Where Matthews came to the UFC as an undefeated 19-year-old prospect, “Chidi Chidi Bang Bang” was the eternal journeyman, bouncing around Bellator MMA and several high-level regional promotions before landing a surprising berth on Dana White's Contender Series in 2021. Already 33 years old at the time of his UFC debut, Njokuani turned heads by knocking out his first two opponents in the first round, including a 16-second blitzing of the normally durable Marc-Andre Barriault. The feel-good story came crashing back to the ground with a three-fight skid, but Njokuani responded by dropping to welterweight, where he has rattled off three straight wins coming into Saturday’s showdown. The Las Vegan’s game remains as simple, yet difficult to solve, as ever. At 6-foot-3 and with a lanky frame—especially by welterweight standards—Njokuani excels as a kickboxer so long as he can dictate the range: all the way out, where his long, straight jab and kicks can do damage, or all the way in, where he can punish his foe with knees in the clinch. While he has a black belt in Brazilian jiu-jitsu, he prefers to spend as little time on the ground as possible, and the good grapplers who have been able to get him down early in a fight have tended to dominate him, going back to his fight with John Salter in Bellator. This fight boils down to two related, but distinct questions: Can Matthews take Njokuani down, and will he try often enough? Even if Matthews does not have immediate success wrestling, it behooves him to try and try again, as that will give Njokuani one more thing to think about on the feet. Matthews is perfectly capable of winning a fight in which he goes three for 14 on takedown attempts; it will be cause to worry if he goes one for his first three and then quits trying. This is a close matchup, as evidenced by the betting line, but the pick is that Njokuani will remain upright enough, and pepper the Aussie with enough jabs and low kicks, to get his hand raised after 15 fun minutes. Njokuani by decision. Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani Jake Matthews (20-7 MMA, 14-7 UFC) makes his 22nd octagon appearance, the most by any Australian-born fighter in company history. Matthews is 10-4 since he moved up to the UFC welterweight division in November 2017. Chidi Njokuani (25-10 MMA, 5-3 UFC) is 3-0 since he dropped to the UFC welterweight division in March 2024. Njokuani's 16-second victory at UFC Fight Night 200 marked the second-fastest debut in UFC middleweight history behind Marc Weir’s 10-second win at UFC 38. Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura Lauren Murphy (16-6 MMA, 8-6 UFC) returns to competition for the first time since Jan. 21, 2023. The 903-day layoff is longest of her more than 15-year career. Kennedy Nzechukwu vs. Valter Walker Kennedy Nzechukwu (14-5 MMA, 8-5 UFC) is 2-0 since he moved up to the heavyweight division in October. Nzechukwu earned a knockout at UFC 259 despite a -64 deficit in significant strikes landed, the biggest statistical comeback for a light heavyweight bout and third overall in UFC history. Valter Walker (13-1 MMA, 2-1 UFC) is one of four heavyweights in UFC history to earn a submission victory by heel hook. He accomplished the feat at UFC 305. title: Preview: UFC Nashville Prelims - Matthews vs. Njokuani
text: Preview: UFC Nashville Prelims Matthews vs. Njokuani Welterweights Jake Matthews (21-7, 14-7 UFC) vs. Chidi Njokuani (25-10, 1 NC; 5-3 UFC)ODDS: Njokuani (-150); Matthews (+125) Advertisement In broad strokes, Matthews’ game remains the same as it ever was. He is a strong and savvy grappler who is capable everywhere but does his best work from top position, and while his striking shows decent power and has improved incrementally over the years, it remains awkward-looking and defensively porous. That being the case, Matthews’ fights tend to hinge on who is the better wrestler, as takedowns are an important safety valve for when things are not going his way on the feet, and present his best chance to get the fight to the ground in the time, place and position of his choosing. It is a fairly straightforward calculus of victory that Matthews sometimes makes more complicated by underusing his wrestling. Njokuani is, in many ways, the polar opposite of Matthews. Where Matthews came to the UFC as an undefeated 19-year-old prospect, “Chidi Chidi Bang Bang” was the eternal journeyman, bouncing around Bellator MMA and several high-level regional promotions before landing a surprising berth on Dana White's Contender Series in 2021. Already 33 years old at the time of his UFC debut, Njokuani turned heads by knocking out his first two opponents in the first round, including a 16-second blitzing of the normally durable Marc-Andre Barriault. The feel-good story came crashing back to the ground with a three-fight skid, but Njokuani responded by dropping to welterweight, where he has rattled off three straight wins coming into Saturday’s showdown. The Las Vegan’s game remains as simple, yet difficult to solve, as ever. At 6-foot-3 and with a lanky frame—especially by welterweight standards—Njokuani excels as a kickboxer so long as he can dictate the range: all the way out, where his long, straight jab and kicks can do damage, or all the way in, where he can punish his foe with knees in the clinch. While he has a black belt in Brazilian jiu-jitsu, he prefers to spend as little time on the ground as possible, and the good grapplers who have been able to get him down early in a fight have tended to dominate him, going back to his fight with John Salter in Bellator. This fight boils down to two related, but distinct questions: Can Matthews take Njokuani down, and will he try often enough? Even if Matthews does not have immediate success wrestling, it behooves him to try and try again, as that will give Njokuani one more thing to think about on the feet. Matthews is perfectly capable of winning a fight in which he goes three for 14 on takedown attempts; it will be cause to worry if he goes one for his first three and then quits trying. This is a close matchup, as evidenced by the betting line, but the pick is that Njokuani will remain upright enough, and pepper the Aussie with enough jabs and low kicks, to get his hand raised after 15 fun minutes. Njokuani by decision.
